title: Establish decision-staircase and tie-breaker protocol for PRD review handoffs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Multiple PRDs in the roadmap have suffered delays because design, engineering, and legal sign-offs diverge on different interpretation paths. This ticket defines a lightweight 'decision staircase'—an ordered escalation and tie-breaker protocol that (1) surfaces scope ambiguities early, (2) documents decision rationale, and (3) provides a clear path for closure when stakeholders cannot reach consensus within the review window.

Objectives:
- Define who can make a final decision at each escalation step (PM -> Eng Tech Lead -> Design Lead -> Legal Counsel -> Head of Product).
- Standardize the artifacts required at each step (PRD section, linked Figma frames, risk summary, compliance note, prototype link, cost/latency impact estimate).
- Set timeboxes for each escalation ladder (48h for initial review, 72h for technical assessment, 5 business days for legal).
- Enumerate tie-breaker rules for three classes of disputes: safety/regulatory, user-experience regressions, and infra/cost trade-offs.
- Produce a one-page template and incorporate it into PRD templates and the PRD review checklist in Confluence.

Scope: This ticket covers process definition, stakeholder RACI, example decision templates, and a small pilot across two upcoming PRDs (structured-output change and dedicated autoscale policy). Operational enforcement (console gating) is out of scope for this ticket and will be tracked separately.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict gating increases velocity friction but reduces rework and downstream incidents. We opted for short timeboxes and explicit fallback owners to balance speed vs. alignment.
- Centralized tie-breaker (Head of Product) reduces back-and-forth but risks single-point bias; we add a 'context packet' requirement to mitigate.

Deliverables:
- Decision staircase runbook (one-pager + examples).
- PRD template updates (Decision Log section).
- Acceptance checklist updates in Confluence and a short training deck for PM/Design/Eng leads.
- Pilot signoff on two PRDs and a retrospective note with metrics (time-to-decision, number of escalations, blocked days avoided).
